title: Back-Rank Mates
subtitle: A trapped king behind its own pawns is a target.

steps.say: The pawn shield that keeps a castled king safe has one fatal flaw: it also blocks his escape. If the back rank isn't guarded, a single rook or queen check is instant checkmate. This pattern wins — and loses — more games than any other tactic in chess.

steps.prompt: Black's rook wandered off to grab pawns. Punish the abandoned back rank — mate in one!
hints: The king's own pawns are his prison bars. Who guards the eighth rank? Nobody.
Send the rook to the back rank — no black piece can reach e8 in time.

line.say: Checkmate! f7, g7 and h7 — Black's own loyal pawns — sealed every exit. The b6 rook watches helplessly from the wrong rank.

rejections.say: Rxe6! You offered your rook on the rank the black rook patrols. The winning rank was the EIGHTH.

steps.wrongSay: The back rank is undefended and the king can't step forward. One rook move ends it.
steps.successSay: When the enemy rook leaves its back rank, that rank becomes your runway.

steps.prompt: Now defend! You're BLACK, and White's queen-rook battery threatens mate on e8. Give your king AIR!
hints: Qe8 would be mate right now — count your king's escape squares: zero. You need 'luft' (air).
Move a shield pawn one step so the king gains an escape hatch.

line.say: Luft! Now Qe8+ is just a check — your king calmly steps to h7. One tiny pawn move defuses the whole battery.
Air for the king via g7 — the back-rank mate threat is permanently cancelled.
The hatch opens on h7 — mate threat neutralized. (h6 is the more standard nudge, but the air is what matters.)

rejections.say: Qe8+! The king walk doesn't escape the battery — the queen arrives with the rook behind her and the attack crashes through anyway. Make luft with a pawn.
Qe8# — checkmate! The a-pawn is on the wrong side of the board. Luft must come from the pawns in front of your KING.

steps.wrongSay: White threatens Qe8#. Only a move that gives your king an escape square (or guards e8) saves you.
steps.successSay: One pawn step — h6 or g6 — inoculates you against the most common checkmate in chess. Cheap insurance!

steps.prompt: Black's c8 rook guards the back rank — but you have TWO attackers on the e-file. Crash through!
hints: Count the e8 square: you attack it twice, Black defends it once. The math says invade.
Play Re8+ — when the guard captures, your second rook recaptures... on the back rank.

line.say: ...and the SECOND rook delivers mate. Two attackers versus one defender — the back rank never stood a chance.

rejections.say: It challenges the guard sideways — but Black just holds with Rd8 or trades on his terms. You outnumber Black on the E-FILE two to one: cash it in with Re8+!

steps.wrongSay: e8 is attacked twice and defended once. Force the trade ON the back rank.
steps.successSay: Defended back ranks fall to arithmetic: more attackers than defenders, then sacrifice first, mate second.

steps.prompt: Danger! Look at YOUR back rank — Black's rook is ready to invade. Find the move that keeps you winning.
hints: Before attacking, always scan your own back rank: Re1+ would be lethal — your queen can't cover e1 forever.
One little pawn move makes your king safe for the rest of the game.

line.say: Air! Re1+ is now met by Kh2, shrugging. With the back rank immune, your extra queen wins effortlessly.
The king gets his escape hatch on g2 — Black's only trick is gone, and your queen cleans up.

rejections.say: Re1+!! and after the forced block Qd1 (the only stopper), Rxd1 is CHECKMATE. You grabbed a pawn while your own back rank was on fire. Luft first — greed later.
It guards e1, but chains your queen to sentry duty forever. One pawn nudge (h3) solves the problem permanently and frees the queen to attack.

steps.wrongSay: Your own back rank is the weakness here. Permanent safety costs one pawn move.
steps.successSay: The final back-rank skill: seeing the threat against YOURSELF. Check your own eighth rank every single move.
